We hypothesize that a key factor in this degradation is the absence of epistemic uncertainty estimation on LLM outputs: the agent has no mechanism to distinguish a high-confidence financial signal from an unreliable hallucination. We query the LLM with N =5 semantically diverse prompts per news article and compute the standard deviation σ across responses; when σ exceeds a threshold τ , the gate closes and the signal is suppressed. We apply this gating mechanism to both the action modifier S f (PPO action perturbation) and the risk modifier R f (CVaR penalty). We evaluate the framework on the FNSPID dataset [Dong et al., 2024] with 28,502 (ticker, date) signals computed via OpenAI gpt-4o-mini, using 10seed evaluation on Nasdaq trading 2019-2023. The gating mechanism achieves the predicted activation rate (34.2% ± 0%, exactly within target [30-40%]) and we demonstrate that LLM uncertainty σ is structurally higher in bear markets (2022: 0.614) than in bull periods (2019: 0.525). Our contribution is a reusable uncertainty-gating mechanism with rigorous multi-seed empirical characterizationrare in this application domain.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6793998\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6877184\", \"title\": [\"Autonomous Negotiation via Deep Reinforcement Learning Agents: Efficiency, Fairness, and Mechanisms\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Business-to-business (B2B) markets power the global economy, yet complex bilateral negotiations often remain slow, fragmented, and inefficient when parties must bargain over multiple issues under private information. Existing market mechanisms rarely solve this tension among efficiency, agility, and privacy. We address this challenge by designing and evaluating an agent-to-agent negotiation framework for multi-issue bilateral exchange. In our setting, autonomous buyer and seller agents hold heterogeneous private preferences and learn adaptive bargaining strategies through self-play reinforcement learning under two-sided incomplete information. The result is striking: near-efficient and fair agreements emerge from decentralized, self-interested interactions without requiring either party to reveal private preferences to the counterparty or a central platform. Across heterogeneous negotiation environments, the agents capture about 91% of the socially optimal surplus in complex multi-issue settings and up to 98% in canonical single-issue benchmarks. We identify two mechanisms behind this performance: interepisode convergence toward reciprocal bargaining strategies and intra-episode inference that helps agents resolve late-stage impasses. We also uncover a counterintuitive boundary condition: payoff observability can undermine, rather than facilitate, cooperation. These findings suggest a core design principle for agentic commerce: privacy preservation and economic efficiency can be complements, not tradeoffs.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6877184\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1093/acprof:oso/9780199283910.003.0003\", \"title\": [\"Political agency and accountability\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1093/acprof:oso/9780199283910.003.0003\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2007, 8, 23]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "71e722a280b645ff4f08baaa4f3af65bbadb7a654389caa726f0e323f21dc30e", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "responsibility_formation", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.35802/227608", "doi:10.2139/ssrn.6793998", "doi:10.2139/ssrn.6877184", "doi:10.1093/acprof:oso/9780199283910.003.0003"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.35802/227608", "https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6793998", "https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6877184", "https://doi.org/10.1093/acprof:oso/9780199283910.003.0003"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}
